years.title: 1980: a terminus with 16 dead-end tracks
years.text: Every train ends here or turns back. Under the forecourt, a first level of shops has existed since 1970.

years.title: 1990: the first through station opens on the north edge
years.text: Museumstrasse station and a new line to the east open for the S-Bahn, the suburban rail network, on 27 May 1990. A two-track terminus for two local lines opens under the forecourt three weeks earlier.

years.title: 2004: a stopgap wing station, and a roof laid in advance
years.text: To free hall tracks for the new national timetable, four S-Bahn lines are moved to four extra dead-end tracks outside the hall. Under the hall, the roof and walls of the next through station are built while the platforms above are being lengthened to 420 m.

years.title: 2014: the second through station opens under the hall
years.text: Löwenstrasse station and the Weinberg tunnel open for the S-Bahn on 15 June 2014. The wing station closes the same day. The bridges to the west are still being built.

years.label: Today
years.title: Since December 2015: long-distance trains run through
years.text: Two bridges to Altstetten complete the 9.6 km cross-city line. Intercity trains between western and eastern Switzerland now pass under the hall without turning back.
